correctness.rationale: For every k>=1 and admissible r_i,a_i,p with r1*r2=q<1<rbar, repeated migration has exact P^k=(1/2)[[1+s,1-s],[1-s,1+s]], s=(1-2p)^k=(-μ)^k. Linearization D P^k has trace rbar(1+s), determinant q s; Perron root Λ(s) is strictly increasing because its differentiated numerator rbar Λ-q stays positive. The unique Λ=1 crossing s=-τ=-(rbar-1)/(rbar-q) lies in (-1,0). Thus all even k endemic and odd k extinct exactly if μ^k>=τ (including equality). For Λ<=1, positive left PF vector yields strict Lyapunov descent (critical case included); for Λ>1 small right-PF subsolution and 1 supersolution with strict subhomogeneity ensure unique positive globally attracting fixed point. Independent 78 exact rational P^k/characteristic/parity tests corroborate; global conclusion proved analytically, not by finite trajectories. Example r1=2,r2=1/5,p=9/10: extinct k=1,3,5,7.
residual_risks: Numerical enumeration is bounded; universal result relies on supplied proof reconstructed above.
